To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the literature on the online teaching roles and competencies does not address the issues of empowerment and critical reflection, and that it lacks a pedagogical approach that integrates technology and learning.

(a) the literature on online teacher roles and competency is limited in its focus on the standards and competencies of teachers; (b) the literature lacks a transformative perspective on online teacher professional development, as it is limited in its exploration of the role of online teachers in promoting empowerment of students, promoting critical reflection of online teachers, and integrating technology in pedagogical inquiry; (c) an alternative perspective on online teacher roles, competencies, and professional development is suggested that considers online teachers as
online teaching literature has not sufficiently addressed the need for online teachers' empowerment, critical reflection and technology integration in their professional development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new vision of online teacher professional development that is grounded in a transformative learning theory perspective.
the professional development of the online teacher as an adult learner, who transforms his or her meaning of structures related online teaching through a process of critical reflection.
the development of an understanding of online teachers as transformative adult learners who continuously construct their professional identity and practice through the process of critical reflection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the literature on the professional development of the online teacher is not comprehensive enough to address the needs of online teachers as transformative learners.
the literature on online teaching roles and competencies is limited in its ability to guide the professional development of the online teacher as a transformative adult learner.
the literature on online teaching roles and competencies is limited by a narrow and technologically deterministic vision of online teaching.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

online teacher preparation and professional development programs should focus on the empowerment and critical reflection of teachers as adult learners in order to transform their online teaching practice.
the literature on online teacher roles and competency lacks in the area of transformative learning and critical reflection, and that this is an important area to be further explored.
we are not suggesting that standards and competencies are unimportant, but we are suggesting that they are insufficient to address the complexities of online teaching.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the online teaching literature needs to be reoriented to address the needs of online teachers as learners who are capable of transforming their practice.

the professional development of teachers should be grounded in a transformative learning approach, which is based on the assumption that learning is a continuous process of reflection and action that leads to changes in meaning.
the professional development of the online teacher should be guided by the principles of transformative learning theory.
